title: Run Dora as systemd units with its CLI as oneshot units
body:
Under systemd, Dora's coordinator and daemon now run as units of the run, and its commands (status, start graph, list, down) run as short-lived units too.
Validation: all 5 native systemd tests pass twice as root (systemd 255, x86_64, dora-cli 1.1.0); unit tests, Clippy, fmt. ARM64 and full CI not run.

First slice of Milestone 4 in the [launch forms plan](https://github.com/Cutuy/doramcap/blob/feature/launch-forms-systemd-dora/libs/workload-lifecycle/docs/110726-launch-forms.md), stacked on #198.

- A plan may include Dora: an executable, two loopback ports, an optional graph and a private runtime directory.
- The coordinator and daemon start before every app group. Readiness asks `dora status` until the daemon reports running, as Compose does.
- Each Dora command runs as a oneshot unit in the run's slice and writes its output to a file in the runtime directory, so nothing runs outside systemd.
- On stop, `dora down` stops the dataflow before the coordinator and daemon stop.

Still to come in Milestone 4: on-demand app binaries from release assets, Console resolving and running systemd plans, and shared-memory ownership.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comments.author: Cutuy
comments.body:
Confirmed. A hung Dora CLI can still block shutdown. The timeout implementation was reverted in 608ea1b because its added complexity was disproportionate for the temporary CLI integration.

PR #210 contains the plan to replace CLI control commands with direct async API calls across Compose and systemd, including explicit deadlines and cancellation handling. It is a plan only; this issue remains open until that behavior is implemented and validated.
